sections.content: When telling a story about the past, you alternate between the two tenses. The imperfecto paints the background; the indefinido moves the plot forward.

items.es: Era de noche. Llovía. De repente, escuché un ruido extraño.
items.en: It was night. It was raining. Suddenly, I heard a strange noise.

items.es: La calle estaba vacía cuando vi a un hombre corriendo.
items.en: The street was empty when I saw a man running.

items.es: Hacía mucho frío. Me puse el abrigo y salí de casa.
items.en: It was very cold. I put on my coat and left the house.

sections.content: A simple writing technique: start every scene with 2–3 imperfecto sentences to set atmosphere, then switch to indefinido for the sequence of events. This mirrors how native speakers naturally tell stories.
